card.band: 8 h. Well-formedness is easy; the long tail (entity recursion, external entities, validity constraints, XML 1.1 edge rules, edition-specific name chars) separates runs. Buckets: not-wf, valid, invalid, namespace, canonical output. A weaker model stops at a well-formedness-only parser.
card.cheat: Wrapping a system libxml2/expat or a bundled XML library: the image has no XML parser libraries beyond the language stdlib and the build blocks the dependency. Hidden mutated inputs defeat catalogue memorisation.
card.grading: Hidden slice of the 2586 catalogue entries (not-wf, invalid, valid, error) plus several thousand mutated documents compared against libxml2 verdicts, run on the verifier only. Exact verdict match and byte-exact canonical output; a visible sample of about 150 cases is shipped for self-checking.
card.reference: Own reference written in Rust, with libxml2 (MIT) and expat (MIT) used to cross-check verdicts. Reference size about 3-5k lines. It would pass all but the cases where the parsers legitimately differ, which are excluded.
card.source: https://www.w3.org/XML/Test/xmlts20130923.tar.gz @ xmlts20130923; licence mixed (James Clark part: unmodified redistribution only; Sun/OASIS/IBM parts separate notices), no single SPDX. Licence must be cleared before shipping; fallback is to ship only the W3C/OASIS-noticed subsets.
card.task: /app ships an empty C or Rust crate with a CLI that reads an XML file and reports well-formed/not-well-formed/valid/invalid, then emits Canonical XML. The agent builds a non-validating-plus-validating parser covering DTD internal/external subsets, parameter/general entities, attribute normalisation, XML 1.1 name/char rules and namespaces.
card.title: Validating XML 1.0 and 1.1 parser with DTD and entities

source_notes: XML 1.0 parser with DTD + entities + validity is a big, rule-dense job with crisp pass/fail; licence mix is the blocker (James Clark clause); moderate crowding because XML parsers are a classic exercise

facts.claim: W3C XML conformance suite release xmlts20130923 exists and is offered as a tar.gz from the W3C test page
The suite contains over 2000 test files
W3C test-suite page or FAQ states a licence for the test cases; FAQ says contributed materials are governed by the W3C Software License (19980720)
James Clark part is 'unmodified redistribution only'; Sun/OASIS/IBM separate notices exist
A public pure-Rust XML crate (rusty_xml) describes itself as a remake of libxml2 with DTD internal subset support and xmlValidateDocument
libxml2 verdicts are a sound oracle for XML 1.1 edge rules
Reference implementation of about 3-5k lines in Rust exists

full_card.band: 8 h tier. Well-formedness is the easy floor; DTD validity, entity recursion, XML 1.1 rules and byte-exact C14N form the long tail. Buckets: not-wf, valid, invalid, namespace, canonical. Weaker model likely stops at well-formedness only. No dated public evidence of agent results.
full_card.build_cost: About 3-5k lines of reference plus a libxml2/expat differential harness and mutation generator: roughly 4-5 days for us (score 2).
full_card.deliverable: CLI binary plus parser crate covering DTD internal/external subsets, parameter/general entities, attribute normalisation, XML 1.1 name/char rules, namespaces, canonical output.
full_card.gates_anticheat: Verifier-only oracle and mutated set; cheat paths: wrapping a system libxml2/expat (spike must confirm absent in image via ldconfig/find), vendoring a Rust XML crate (block offline build and check Cargo.lock), editing tests or build config (verifier uses own copy).
full_card.grading_surface: Hidden slice of catalogue entries (not-wf, invalid, valid, error) plus several thousand mutated documents, compared to libxml2 verdicts with byte-exact canonical output; about 150 visible cases shipped. Exact count 2586 unverified; 'over 2000' confirmed.
full_card.local_fit: Rust or C, CPU only, offline build; fits 8 cores, 16 GB, gVisor; no kernel features needed.
full_card.lookup: Partial: libxml2 and expat are famous C implementations a frontier model knows in outline; rusty_xml is a public pure-Rust libxml2 remake with DTD validation, not installable offline; no direct solution found.
full_card.provenance: W3C XML Conformance Test Suite xmlts20130923 (OASIS-origin XML 1.0 2nd ed. suite plus IBM/Sun/James Clark contributions); real spec and suite; no git history, smoke probe skipped (no git source).
full_card.reference: Own Rust reference, about 3-5k lines, not yet written; libxml2 and expat (both MIT) as cross-check oracles; legitimately differing cases excluded.
full_card.ships: Empty C or Rust crate with a CLI for well-formed/not-well-formed/valid/invalid verdicts and Canonical XML output; no XML parser library in the image (to verify in spike).
full_card.similarity: Nearest l0 neighbours S-im-044 (0.228), S-im-038 (0.213), S-im-045 (0.161) are above the 0.15 novelty line. libexpat is on the CROWDED list, and XML parsing is adjacent to crowded JSON/YAML parser work.

Band.why: Frontier 8 h plausibly reaches well-formed plus part of validity, but no dated public evidence; capped at 3 without it.

Build.why: Reference of 3-5k lines plus differential harness is about 4-5 days for us.

Fit.why: CPU-only Rust or C with offline build; no special kernel features.

Hor.why: 8 h tier justified by several interacting modules (DTD, entities, namespaces, C14N, XML 1.1).

Lic.why: No single SPDX; James Clark clause (unmodified redistribution only) unverified and blocks shipping derived mutated tests until cleared.

Multi.why: Five named buckets (not-wf, valid, invalid, namespace, canonical) give steady partial credit.

Nov.why: Neighbour 0.228 above the 0.15 line and libexpat is on the CROWDED list.

Real.why: Real W3C suite release and spec; reference and suite licensing still unresolved so not 5.

Ref.why: Own reference not yet written; libxml2 verdicts disagree with the spec on some cases, so the oracle is not a clean spec reference.

Seal.why: Suite is public but offline; hidden slice and mutated set stay verifier-side; libxml2 oracle is public but not in the image.

Surf.why: Thousands of mutated documents with an executable libxml2 oracle give an unlimited generator.

spike_plan.kill_if: The James Clark clause forbids derived or mutated redistribution and the noticed subset is under 500 cases (K6/K3); libxml2 disagrees with labels on more than 10% of XML 1.1 cases so the oracle is unsound there (K4); or a usable XML library is present in the image and cannot be removed (K11).
spike_plan.pass_if: Licence notices allow shipping unmodified tests and a derived mutated set, or the noticed subset still gives at least 1000 cases; libxml2 agrees with suite labels on at least 95% of non-excluded cases; the image has no XML library; two runs are identical.
steps: In a fresh empty directory under the scratchpad, download and extract xmlts20130923.tar.gz with tar; do not run any script inside it.

List every per-directory README/notice file; record the James Clark, Sun, OASIS and IBM licence wording verbatim and decide which subsets may be shipped unmodified and whether mutated derivatives are allowed.
Count TEST elements in xmlconf.xml by TYPE (not-wf, invalid, valid, error) to test the 2586 figure and the per-bucket sizes.
In a base Debian container matching the /app image, run ldconfig -p and find for expat and xml2 libraries and headers, and check that no Rust XML crate is in the offline cargo cache.
Run xmllint --noout --valid (or --noout) over the valid/invalid/not-wf sets twice and compare outputs for determinism.
Measure libxml2 agreement with the suite TYPE labels per subset, separately for XML 1.0 and XML 1.1 cases.
Decide the exclusion list from the disagreement set and check that each bucket keeps at least about 200 cases.

v1.summary: The XML conformance suite is real and public, but the licence (James Clark clause and the 2586-entry count) is unverified, so shipping and count claims are open. No gate fails outright, so the idea stays alive with licence and oracle soundness as the spike's first checks.
